source_gap_claims.behavior: A Package B handoff table must state the accepted quality contract and CLI, legacy behavior, and expected migration touchpoints for the five Skills.
source_gap_claims.reason: The complete obligation set contains no Package B handoff-table duty.
source_gap_claims.subject: Package B handoff

source_gap_claims.behavior: The handoff must preserve existing authority and keep Bootstrap Review optional.
source_gap_claims.reason: No obligation preserves these authority and lifecycle decisions.
source_gap_claims.subject: Package B handoff

source_gap_claims.behavior: Package A completion gates must not require the five real Skills to pass the new standard or enable an internal reviewer.
source_gap_claims.reason: The obligations do not prohibit either completion-gate dependency.
source_gap_claims.subject: Package A completion gate

source_gap_claims.behavior: BMAD, GDS, and Chapter 2-7 Skills must remain excluded from the Package A scope.
source_gap_claims.reason: No obligation preserves these exclusions.
source_gap_claims.subject: Package A scope

source_gap_claims.behavior: Implement one capability-aware, read-only local package validator that checks package declarations and structure, never grants execution permissions, never runs a Skill, and does not establish runtime security or product acceptance.
source_gap_claims.reason: The obligations specify individual validation rules but do not establish this validator authority boundary.
source_gap_claims.subject: Package A validator

source_gap_claims.behavior: Produce the declared standard document, ADR-0062 and its ADR-index entry, policy JSON, contract and result schemas, and a validator module exposing callable validate_package and argparse main entries.
source_gap_claims.reason: No obligation requires these concrete production deliverables or entrypoints.
source_gap_claims.subject: Production deliverables

source_gap_claims.behavior: The validator must consume the normative policy and schemas as its actual inputs, while the quality sidecar coexists with the existing owner-specific contracts and documents its namespace, frontmatter keys, relative-reference rules, and normalization.
source_gap_claims.reason: Existing obligations validate contract structure but do not require these input-ownership and coexistence rules.
source_gap_claims.subject: Normative inputs and quality namespace

source_gap_claims.behavior: Package A must not add a model, HTTP request, installer, new dependency service, or automatic execution of package-declared commands.
source_gap_claims.reason: No obligation imposes these implementation prohibitions.
source_gap_claims.subject: Implementation scope

source_gap_claims.behavior: Expose the specified repository-root CLI and validate_package API with explicit repository root, package root, policy, and mode; invocation must use an argv contract and a finite positive caller-assigned timeout.
source_gap_claims.reason: The obligations do not require this exact public invocation contract or API parameter boundary.
source_gap_claims.subject: Public invocation contract

source_gap_claims.behavior: CLI output must be one versioned JSON result containing package identity, status, ordered diagnostics, and authorizes as an empty list; exit codes must distinguish pass, noncompliance, invocation/inspection error, and legacy inventory, and diagnostics must omit secrets, absolute host paths, and arbitrary source text.
source_gap_claims.reason: Existing obligations cover general structured output and determinism but omit these result fields, exit-code assignments, and redaction constraints.
source_gap_claims.subject: Validator result contract

source_gap_claims.behavior: The main validator must consume the bounded example/branch helper; static validation must not claim semantic review of example usefulness, and no internal reviewer is required.
source_gap_claims.reason: The obligations check example structure but do not require helper consumption or prohibit unsupported semantic-review claims.
source_gap_claims.subject: Example-checking boundary

source_gap_claims.behavior: Resolve dependencies only from explicitly supplied local records and do not scan all repositories, select a latest-successful log, require knowledge-base publication, or become a knowledge-query workflow.
source_gap_claims.reason: Dependency obligations define declarations and fallback behavior but not this resolution-source restriction.
source_gap_claims.subject: Dependency resolution scope

source_gap_claims.behavior: Capability validation must prove only declaration presence and internal consistency, name the owning runtime entrypoints, avoid claiming runtime enforcement, and conditionally require controls only for capabilities actually declared, including composed capabilities.
source_gap_claims.reason: The obligations do not define this runtime-authority disclaimer or composed-capability conditionality.
source_gap_claims.subject: Capability authority boundary

source_gap_claims.behavior: Clean package validation must validate the actual published policy and schemas against the reference package and retain external review of the normative standard; the Markdown standard is not an installed Skill and must not cause a governance Skill to be invented.
source_gap_claims.reason: No obligation requires this terminal validation interpretation or prevents creation of a governance Skill.
source_gap_claims.subject: Reference-package validation

source_gap_claims.behavior: Test helpers must use disposable fixture roots; corruptions and synthetic credentials are test data; tests must invoke the real validator or CLI, compare structured diagnostics and boundary effects, and fail if the validator is replaced by an unconditional pass implementation.
source_gap_claims.reason: The obligations do not require these fixture-isolation and anti-stub verification duties.
source_gap_claims.subject: Validator test integrity

source_gap_claims.behavior: Run the declared four-module pytest terminal selection, and make its integration test invoke the published CLI with a literal argv list, shell=false, repository cwd, and finite timeout, parse fresh JSON against the result schema, and verify reference-pass/mutated-reject behavior.
source_gap_claims.reason: No obligation specifies this repository-owned terminal command or integration-test oracle.
source_gap_claims.subject: Terminal acceptance

source_gap_claims.behavior: Package A changes must remain limited to the standard, validator, reference fixtures, and migration guidance, with the listed Phase, runtime, authentication, shared-entrypoint, knowledge, historical, and other protected paths left unchanged.
source_gap_claims.reason: The obligations do not impose the repair's production allowlist and protected-path exclusions.
source_gap_claims.subject: Scope and protected paths

source_gap_claims.behavior: ADR-0062 must be checked for path collision, proposed during drafting, and accepted through the normal maintainer decision before being cited as implementation authority; a draft must not be marked accepted merely to satisfy tests.
source_gap_claims.reason: No obligation governs ADR collision handling or acceptance status.
source_gap_claims.subject: ADR lifecycle

source_gap_claims.behavior: Use the self-hosted VDD mode with development governance off, preserve historical material without treating it as current, and do not add current attestations, reviewer signatures, Bootstrap receipts, authorization receipts, or a new report.
source_gap_claims.reason: The obligations contain no VDD-mode or historical-evidence governance constraints.
source_gap_claims.subject: VDD governance

source_gap_claims.behavior: Only scripts/vdd/compile_plan.py may publish the current semantic plan and plan-ready state, and compiler output must cover every behavior with acceptance, oracle, assertions, source references, and failure intent while checking structural and scope constraints explicitly.
source_gap_claims.reason: No obligation assigns publication authority or requires complete compiler coverage and structural checks.
source_gap_claims.subject: Semantic-plan publication

source_gap_claims.behavior: Runtime-bearing obligations must use the current CER behavior-routing intent; Quick Dev must assign present, missing, or unverifiable only after controlled execution, and present behavior must remain in regression or terminal coverage.
source_gap_claims.reason: The obligations do not define CER routing or Quick Dev status authority.
source_gap_claims.subject: Execution-status authority

source_gap_claims.behavior: Every executable failure intent must name a planned pytest selector, real production entry, expected observable AssertionError, and bounded validation command; missing modules, imports, environment failures, and absent planned tests are not causal RED.
source_gap_claims.reason: No obligation requires this failure-intent metadata or excludes infrastructure failures from RED causality.
source_gap_claims.subject: Failure-intent binding

source_gap_claims.behavior: Q2 may author only declared tests, helpers, fixtures, and real-entry bindings; when a valid oracle cannot be constructed, the contract must be repaired rather than using a mock product or writing production before the allowed stage.
source_gap_claims.reason: The obligations do not constrain Q2 authoring or prohibit mock-product and premature-production work.
source_gap_claims.subject: Q2 authoring boundary

source_gap_claims.behavior: Tests, helpers, fixture bytes, selectors, the plan, and Acceptance must freeze before formal RED; implementation workers may change only declared production owners and may not review, accept, commit, or merge their own output.
source_gap_claims.reason: No obligation defines these freeze and worker-independence controls.
source_gap_claims.subject: Execution ownership

source_gap_claims.behavior: Shared production dependency changes must invalidate affected proofs; Q6 must have a nonempty applicable regression list and Q8 must perform one current whole-plan terminal validation.
source_gap_claims.reason: The obligations do not require proof invalidation or these Q6/Q8 gates.
source_gap_claims.subject: Regression and terminal gates

source_gap_claims.behavior: The compiler may split atomic behavior lanes but must not merge independent oracles or omit any A01-A25 intent or either NFR constraint.
source_gap_claims.reason: No obligation preserves this compiler coverage and oracle-separation rule.
source_gap_claims.subject: Compiler lane coverage

source_gap_claims.behavior: Enforce the declared production and Q2 allowlists, permit Q2 only the specified fixture categories, keep frozen tests and fixtures immutable during green/refactor, and reject broad scripts/sc, docs/adr, or .agents/skills write sets.
source_gap_claims.reason: The obligations do not define these file-write allowlists or immutability rules.
source_gap_claims.subject: Write-set control

source_gap_claims.behavior: Provide one primary pytest case named test_a01 through test_a25 in its group owner, use explicit parameter IDs, execute every parameter instance, bind exact CER assertion IDs, call the real validator or CLI, and use explicit non-RED artifact assertions for documentary constraints.
source_gap_claims.reason: No obligation requires this exact case naming, execution, assertion binding, or documentary-constraint treatment.
source_gap_claims.subject: Case and assertion mapping

source_gap_claims.behavior: Targeted commands must be limited to the relevant group and predecessors, with 300-second targeted and 900-second terminal timeouts; a timeout is a harness failure, never accepted RED or evidence of security denial.
source_gap_claims.reason: The obligations do not specify command scope, timeout values, or timeout classification.
source_gap_claims.subject: Command bounds

source_gap_claims.behavior: Retain failure evidence, repair only the affected group and dependents, invalidate proofs after shared policy/schema/validator changes, stabilize targeted checks before terminal replay, and route missing or changed sources to contract repair rather than publication, Bootstrap, new lineage, or out-of-scope patches.
source_gap_claims.reason: No obligation defines this repair and evidence-preservation workflow.
source_gap_claims.subject: Repair workflow
